upgrades.text: You also find 1 Rank damage die's-worth of Misc. Junk.
A Dumpster Dive takes 30 minutes. On a Critical Hit, you gain an additional interesting item.
A Dumpster Dive takes 10 minutes. On an Amazing Success, you gain an interesting item.

name: Endurance
desc: Use this Skill to prevent fatigue while grinding, walking long distances (measured in miles), or other extended strenuous activities. Make an Unopposed Skill Check. On Success, you may continue the activity and do not gain the Fatigued Debuff.

upgrades.text: You can ignore the effects of a Major Fail when making these Checks.
If you are not Fatigued or in extreme conditions, you make this Check with Advantage.
If your Check is a Critical Fail, you can take the effects of a Standard Fail.

name: Engineering
limitations: Cannot create vehicles or high-powered engines (see Gear Head, p. 192).
desc: This Skill is used to design and build things with moving parts, fluids, or chemicals wholly out of Misc. Junk with no inherent bonuses, though they may have situational bonuses. Examples include a watch, a water pump, or bullets (see Crafting, p. 221). Starting on the Fourth Floor, you may make use of an Engineering Table to make your mundane items easier to craft. Make an Unopposed Skill Check. On Success, you create the item.

upgrades.text: Choose a mundane item type to specialize in. You have Advantage when creating an item of that type.
You may craft your specialty item with a +1 bonus level enchantment.
You may craft your specialty item with up to +2 bonus level enchantment, and it takes half the time.

name: Escape Artist
desc: You're especially skilled at the art of escape. When trying to escape bonds, make an Unopposed Skill Check. To escape being Held, make a STR-Opposed Skill Check. Based on the complexity or simplicity of what binds you, the GM may have you make the Check with Advantage or Disadvantage. On Success, you escape your bonds or the creature holding you.

upgrades.text: You can escape your bonds, and no one sees you do it. If you escape being Held, you can then take a Step (also unseen).
When other crawlers in your party roll this skill untrained, they roll as normal (not with Disadvantage).
When you slip out, you may immediately take an Action with Advantage.

name: Escape Plan
limitations: Ranks in this Skill only advance by magical means.
desc: Your HUD reveals hidden doors and passages, unless those passages were crafted by someone with more Ranks in Fabricate or Engineering than you have in this Skill or the passage is entirely natural.

upgrades.text: You have access to system-concealed displays and the Dungeon Locator. Holographic signs pop up in your HUD, displaying insider information like signs at a zoo, including arrows toward City and stronger Bosses.
You are able to read hidden sigils (glowing blue circles) used by the showrunners to direct the movement of Mobs.
You are able to read hidden messages and redactions in dungeon documents.

name: Explosives Handling
desc: For making Attack Skill Checks with explosives (see Throwing, p. 200). Make an Unopposed Skill Check. On Success, you safely handle standard explosive devices. On Fail, the GM will think of something.

upgrades.text: You are able to determine the type, status, and raw materials of explosives you handle.
You are able to craft explosives such as dynamite as if this were a crafting Skill, though you must have explosive raw materials and a Sapper's Table (see Crafting, p. 221).
You may create explosive raw materials out of non-volatile materials. Your crafting takes half the time.

name: Fabricate
limitations: Cannot create things with moving parts, fluids, or chemicals.
desc: Use this Skill to make generic, mundane items with no inherent bonuses wholly out of Misc. Junk, but your GM can give them situational bonuses. Examples include a ladder, a 50ft rope, or a ceramic pot. For items with moving parts, see Engineering (see Crafting, p. 221). Make an Unopposed Skill Check. On Success, you create the item.

upgrades.text: Choose a mundane item to specialize in. You have Advantage when creating that item.
You may craft your specialty item with a +1 bonus level enchantment.
You may craft your specialty item with up to +2 bonus level enchantment, and it takes half the time.

name: Find Crawler
limitations: Ranks in this Skill only increase by magical means.
desc: Your HUD displays other crawlers within 1,000 feet of you. They are designated with a blue dot.

upgrades.text: The area in which you can detect other crawlers increases to 5 miles.
The area in which you can detect other crawlers increases to 10 miles.
You can input a specific crawler's name and learn their exact location anywhere in the dungeon.

name: Find Trap
limitations: Ranks in this Skill only increase by magical means and training.
desc: Traps within 5 feet of you appear on your HUD one second prior to triggering the trap, which is often too late to react.

upgrades.text: Traps appear on your HUD up to 5 seconds before they are triggered.
Traps within 10 feet of you appear on your HUD as you approach them.
Traps within 15 feet of you appear on your HUD as you approach them.

name: First Aid
limitations: After you treat someone, you can't treat them again until they complete a Short or Long Rest.
desc: Give minor medical aid to yourself or someone else. Make an Unopposed Skill Check. On Success, the patient regains 1 Health Bar slot. Each higher degree of Success heals 1 additional slot.

upgrades.text: If you spend 5 minutes, the patient also heals a Minor Injury Debuff.
If you spend 10 minutes, the patient also heals a Long-Term Minor Injury Debuff.
The patient regains 1 additional Health Bar slot. If you spend 15 minutes, the patient also heals a Major Injury Debuff.

name: Gear Head
limitations: This Limited Skill can only be learned via a Race, Class, or item. Requires an Engine Stand attachment to an Engineering Table (2,000 gold).
desc: You are proficient at building high-performance engines, using the rules of Crafting (see p. 221). Each +5ft Move is a +1 Bonus Level at the default '10 + Bonus Level x4' Difficulty. The time it takes and Misc. Junk required uses the rules of crafting mundane items. On Success, you have successfully built a custom engine.

upgrades.text: You are able to add accessories to vehicles or even build your own custom vehicles. Use the rules of Engineering, but use this Skill and there are no bonus level limits to your custom-crafted items.
Each +10ft Move is a +1 Bonus Level. You may use this Skill as a Repair Skill (see p. 197) when fixing engines.
Cut the time required to craft engines and vehicles you build around your engines in half.

name: Goblin Explosives
desc: For making Attack Skill Checks with explosives (see Throwing, p. 200). Make an Unopposed Skill Check. Goblin Explosives are so unstable that Critical Fails occur on a Natural 1-4. On Success, you safely use Goblin Explosive devices.

upgrades.text: Critical Fail occurs on a Natural 3 or less. You are able to determine the type, status, and raw materials of Goblin Explosives you handle.

Critical Fail occurs on a Natural 2 or less. You are able to craft explosives such as dynamite as if this were a crafting Skill, though you must have explosive raw materials and a Sapper's Table (see Crafting, p. 221).
Critical Fail occurs on a Natural 1 as usual. You may create explosive raw materials out of non-volatile materials with the use of a Sapper's Table. Your crafting takes half the time.

name: Good First Impression
limitations: Doesn't work on crawlers, Bosses, or Elites. You can only make a Skill Check against individuals, not groups.
desc: When you encounter an NPC or Mob that is not immediately hostile or attacking, make an INT-Opposed Skill Check. On Success, the Mob approaches with wary curiosity.

upgrades.text: A Mob that is lower level than you won't attack your party unless they are attacked by a member of your party.
A Mob that is up to double your level won't attack your party unless they are attacked by you or an ally or your party is preventing them from completing their objective.
A group of Mobs of the same type up to double your level won't attack your party unless they are attacked by a member of your party, or your party is preventing them from completing their objective.

name: Hide in Shadows
limitations: To move while avoiding detection, see Stealth (p. 199).
desc: While in a heavily shadowed area or out of sight, you can stay still and attempt to foil foes' chances to spot you. Make an INT-Opposed Skill Check. If you're hiding behind an object that is larger than you, roll with Advantage. On Success, you become invisible to Mobs and the HUDs of other crawlers but can still be affected by environmental and Area Attacks. You become visible if you take an Action that affects another creature or if you're no longer behind cover.

upgrades.text: You can use this Skill in a dim light without having an object to hide behind.
When other crawlers in your party roll this Skill untrained, they roll as normal (not with Disadvantage).
You can use this Skill in a lightly shaded area and may make a Step without giving away your position.

name: Improvised Explosive Device
desc: Use this Skill to manipulate explosive material into bombs and traps without a Sapper's Table. You'll have to make an Explosives Handling Skill Check to avoid issues when crafting your device (use the rules of Crafting, p. 221). On Success, you create the device. Bombs and traps can have timers and triggering devices more sophisticated than a burning fuse.

upgrades.text: Your crafting takes half the time.
Your devices deal d10s of damage instead of d6s (the default).
Your devices can be set to trigger only against a specific Mob, Boss, NPC, or crawler.

name: Incendiary Device Handling
desc: For making Attack Skill Checks with incendiary devices (see Throwing, p. 200). Make an Unopposed Skill Check. On Success, you are able to safely handle incendiary devices.

upgrades.text: You are able to determine the type, status, and raw materials of incendiary devices you handle.
You are able to craft incendiary devices as if this were a crafting Skill, though you must have incendiary raw materials and a Sapper's Table (see Crafting, p. 221).
Add a +5 Splash to your crafted device at no additional Difficulty, and your crafting takes half the time.

name: Infusion
limitations: Requires an Infusion Station attachment on an Alchemy Table or Tier 3 Sapper's Table.
desc: Use this Skill to infuse potion bonuses onto consumable items. One potion can infuse one item. You'll either need to learn Alchemy to craft your own potions, or find potions to transfer to consumables. Example: Infuse a Hobgoblin Smoke Curtain with an Invisibility potion to create a Hobgoblin Disco Ball (see Crafting, p. 221). On Success, your consumable item now does more.

upgrades.text: One potion can infuse 2 items at once.
One potion can infuse 5 items at once.
One potion can infuse 10 items at once.

name: Intimidate
desc: You can use this Skill to scare the wits out of a foe. Make a CHA-Opposed Skill Check. If either side has attacked or taken a hostile stance in this encounter, roll with Disadvantage. On Success, the target gains the Staggered Debuff (p. 97).

upgrades.text: On Success or greater, until the end of the next round, the target can only use its remaining Actions to move away from you (though it does not need to use its Step when doing so).
The target also gains the Woozy Debuff.
The target drops everything they were holding and also gains the Paralyzed Debuff.

name: Investigation
desc: You spend 10 minutes looking at an area or puzzle in front of you and might make heads or tails of it. Make an Unopposed Skill Check. When you take the Look for Clues Action (p. 85), spend only one Action to use this Skill. On Success, you learn something useful.

upgrades.text: If you're familiar with the area you are investigating, you can make the Skill Check with Advantage.
Each attempt takes 5 minutes.
Roll with Advantage if you know the parties involved. Example: You know the puzzle's maker, or you know the murder victim and the main suspect.

name: Iron Stomach
desc: Eat magic items for fun and profit! But beware of cursed items, as they could have negative effects. Make an Unopposed Skill Check. On Success, you eat the item and it is destroyed. On an Amazing Success or better, gain 1 permanent Intelligence.

upgrades.text: On a Critical Hit, gain 1 additional permanent Intelligence.
On a Standard Success or better, gain 1 permanent Intelligence. You may eat cursed items with no ill effects.
You choose which Stat is permanently increased.

name: Jumping
desc: With a running start of at least 10 feet (made as a 10-foot Step with this Action), you leap through the air in an arcing trajectory. Make an Unopposed Skill Check. On Success, you leap a distance in feet up to your Rank + STR with a height of 1ft.

upgrades.text: Add your DEX to the height of your Jump.
You gain a +1 Evade Buff.
Your leap distance in feet is Rank + [STR x2].

name: Leadership
desc: You are skilled at coordinating two or more separate parties during fights against Bosses. Make an INT-Opposed Skill Check. On Success, the parties have Advantage on their first Attack against the Boss.

upgrades.text: You may instead use this Skill during Skill challenges while on a group Quest. Perform a free Call a Play Action, and it extends to each member of the parties during their next non-combat Skill Check.
Instead of Advantage, anyone in the parties may perform a free Move Action.
Instead of Advantage, anyone in the parties may perform a free Evade Action.

name: Light on Your Feet
limitations: Usable only by animals.
desc: With a running start of at least 10 feet (made as a 10ft Step with this Skill), you leap through the air in an arcing trajectory. Make an Unopposed Skill Check. On Success, you leap a distance in feet up to your Rank x2 with a height equal to your DEX x2 in feet.

upgrades.text: Your distance is Rank x3 and your height is DEX x3.
You may leap without an arcing trajectory, which allows for 'straight up.'
Your leap may last up to your Rank in seconds, which resembles gliding.

name: Lockpicking
limitations: Roll with Disadvantage if you do not have the proper tools, unless it's a crude lock.
desc: You spend the Floor number in minutes trying to pick the lock. Make an Unopposed Skill Check (more complex locks may have a higher Difficulty, as determined by the GM). If the lock was created by a named antagonist, this could be an INT-Opposed Skill Check instead. On Success, you pick the lock.

upgrades.text: You make no noise and leave no trace.
Each attempt takes half the time. You may alter the lock so that the key no longer works.
You don't roll with Disadvantage if you lack the proper tools.

name: Lore
desc: You have studied the goings-on in the Dungeon and have figured out a thing or two. Make an Unopposed Skill Check. On Success, you know a little something about a neighborhood, some of the Mobs, or how to avoid pissing off the locals.

upgrades.text: You can identify the major factions in the area.
You are aware of the important local NPCs.
You roll with Advantage on your first Charisma-based Skill Check when encountering an organized group in a neighborhood.

name: Negotiation
limitations: Does not work on members of your own party. Some items have a minimum price.
desc: You spend 5 minutes haggling over the price of items or negotiating to get what you want through compromise. Typically, haggling is done with an NPC merchant; if you haggle with other entities, you do so with Disadvantage. Make an INT-Opposed Skill Check. On Success, you increase or decrease the price 10% in your favor. If you're not haggling, the opponent tentatively agrees to your terms.

upgrades.text: Your party members can also buy or sell at your newly-negotiated price.
Increase or decrease the price by an additional 10% in your favor.
Increase or decrease the price by an additional 15% in your favor.

name: Pathfinder
limitations: Ranks in this Skill only increase by magical means and training.
desc: Your HUD map zooms out with a thought, the breadth of which is determined by a multiplier equal to your Rank. Example: Rank 4 means your map covers x4 the standard area (1/4 of a square mile), which makes it extend to 1 mile around you.

upgrades.text: You are notified when you are near a saferoom or stairwell.
You can see through your map while it is open in your HUD.
Mobs appear as red dots on your HUD map.

name: Perception
desc: You concentrate your senses to pick out details about your environment that others might miss. Make an Unopposed Skill Check, though the GM will likely adjust the Difficulty based on the lighting, how cluttered the area is, how quickly an event occurs, and other such circumstances. Also use Perception when you take a Look for Clues Action (p. 85). On Success, you notice something. It could be important; it might not be.

upgrades.text: Halve the penalty for cluttered areas.
Halve the penalty for how short of a window you have to notice the thing.
Halve the penalty for the range to the thing.

name: Performance
desc: Whether you're acting, dancing, playing an instrument, singing, or delivering slam poetry, use this Skill when you want to electrify an audience. Choose a type of performance to specialize in as your starting type. Make an Unopposed Skill Check to determine the audience reaction. If you are competing against other performers, add the top rival's CHA to the Difficulty. On Success, you command the stage. The audience is entertained.

upgrades.text: Choose an additional type of performance to specialize in.

Choose an additional type of performance. You can coach and coordinate others in one of your specialties; after coaching them for at least 1 hour in one of your specialties, they can attempt an unskilled Performance Skill Check without Disadvantage.
Choose an additional type of performance. You can mimic someone else's performance after experiencing it once.

name: Persuasion
desc: You have a knack for getting others to see things your way. You typically need about 10 minutes of schmoozing in a safe environment to make a Check with this Skill, and you may suffer Disadvantage if the request is risky, inconvenient, or untoward. Make an INT-Opposed Skill Check. On Success, you convince the target to follow your suggestion if it isn't too costly for them, too dangerous, or against their nature.

upgrades.text: They'll follow your suggestion even if it is costly for them.
They'll follow your suggestion even if it is dangerous.
They'll follow your suggestion even if it's against their nature.

name: Regeneration
desc: If your Rank in this Skill is equal to or greater than your CON, you heal 1 Health Bar slot at the start of each round (or every 10 seconds outside of combat). If not, you heal 1 Health Bar slot every other round (or every 20 seconds outside of combat).

upgrades.text: After 5 minutes, any Minor Injury Debuff you suffer from ends. After 10 minutes, any Major Injury Debuff you suffer from ends.
After 20 minutes, any Long-Term Minor Injury Debuff you suffer from ends. After 1 hour, any Long-Term Major Injury Debuff you suffer from ends.
The time required to end injury Debuffs is halved.

name: Religion
desc: You have a knack for understanding gods, their followers, and what makes them tick. Make an Unopposed Skill Check. On Success, you know the basic information about a god and the practices of their followers.

upgrades.text: You can identify the followers on sight, even if they're trying to hide their affiliation.
You know how to sow discord among the followers of that religion.
You know strengths and weakness of the gods.

name: Repair
limitations: For basic repairs to items with no moving parts, magical or not.
desc: After spending 2 hours, you can repair most simple items that are broken or damaged but not destroyed. Make an Unopposed Skill Check. On Success, you repair the item.

upgrades.text: You can make repairs to things with moving parts.
You can make repairs in 1 hour.
You can rebuild a destroyed item.

name: Riding
limitations: The rider in control of the mount rolls Attack Skill Checks with Disadvantage.
desc: While mounted on a living beast, you can ride to the local watering hole without needing to make a Check. But during an action scene, your mount might panic, and you might get tossed for 1d6 bludgeoning for every 10ft Move your mount has, plus its size value. Make an Unopposed Skill Check. On Success, your mount doesn't stumble, and you stay upright.

upgrades.text: Your mount has +5ft Move. You no longer suffer Disadvantage when attacking while Riding.
Your mount has an additional +10ft Move. When other crawlers in your party roll this Skill untrained, they roll as normal (not with Disadvantage).
Your mount has an additional +15ft Move. When performing crazy stunts (like jumping through flames), roll with Advantage.

name: Ropework
desc: You know a half hitch from a clove hitch, and the qualities of hemp vs. nylon. This knowledge is used to tie people up, climb, and cattle-rustle. Make an Unopposed Skill Check. On Success, you rope the thing with a good knot.

upgrades.text: You can now use this Skill as an Attack, at a Range of 10ft vs. the target's Evade. On Success, the target gains the Held Debuff.
You can whip your line in that special way to untie a knot you made and recover your rope.
Your Attack now has a Range of your Strength (min 15). Just make sure your rope is long enough.

name: Running
limitations: For short bursts of running. For extended runs, use Endurance instead (p. 190).
desc: If you're racing, chasing, or need to get away from a ticking time bomb, this is the Skill you want (see Racing & Chasing, p. 73). Make an Unopposed Skill Check every minute, not every round. Add 1 to your result for every 10ft of Move you have. On Success, you succeed in the run.

upgrades.text: You have a permanent +5ft Move Buff. Make a Check every 2 minutes.
You have an additional permanent +10ft Move Buff. Make a Check every 4 minutes.
You have an additional permanent +15ft Move Buff. Make a Check every 6 minutes.

name: Salvage
limitations: Salvage cannot be used with explosive devices.
desc: Salvage is the art of collecting useful items from things you have deconstructed or failed to properly craft (see Crafting, p. 221). Salvaging usually takes 1 hour to accomplish. At the end of that time, make an Unopposed Skill Check. On Success, you recover half of the important raw materials.

upgrades.text: Your Salvage Checks take 30 minutes.
On Success, you recover all of the important raw materials.
On a crafting Standard Fail or Near Miss, roll your crafting Check again with Advantage, with an additional 15-minute time expenditure.

name: Scutelliphily
limitations: This Limited Skill can only be learned via a Race, Class, or item.
desc: You know your way around patches and love collecting them. Make an Unopposed Skill Check. On Success, you are able to identify a patch and its bonus level, if any.

upgrades.text: You can sew and iron patches onto clothing using this Skill.
You may use this as a crafting Skill, but crafting tables provide no bonuses. Enchanted patches are limited to one per Gear slot and do not take up Accessory slots (see Crafting, p. 221).

Your crafting Checks take half the time. Increase the bonus value of your enchantments with this Skill by 1, at no additional Difficulty or time to craft. Example: If you craft a +2 Strength patch, it becomes a +3 Strength patch.

name: Shield Block
limitations: Requires you to be wielding a shield. Cannot be used against Area of Effect damage. A successful Shield Block still counts as 'a hit crawler' or 'a crawler who failed to Evade.'
desc: When you are attacked by a physical Attack, spend one Action to make a separate Shield Block Skill Check vs. the Mob's 'to hit' for each of the Attacks targeting you. If 3 physical Attacks are directed at you, roll this Skill Check 3 times. On Success, take half the damage before applying your DR. Your Shield takes a -1 DR penalty on a Major Fail; -2 on a Critical Fail. It breaks at 0 DR, but a broken shield and lost DR can be Repaired.

upgrades.text: You may also use this Skill against Spells and magical damage.
On a Critical Hit, you may make a Shield Bash Attack as a free melee-range Interrupt Attack (instead of Advantage on your next Attack) if you wish, dealing 3d6 base damage + STR Bludgeoning.
+1d6 Shield Bash damage. Further reduce the damage you would take by your STR Mod. Example: After halving 30 damage down to 15, your STR Mod of 5 reduces it to 10 damage.

name: Sleight of Hand
limitations: Items you manipulate must be smaller than the size of your hand. You cannot access others' Inventories or Hotlists.
desc: You've learned to manipulate small objects without being spotted. Great for shoplifting. Make an INT-Opposed Skill Check. If someone's Perception is a higher Rank than your Sleight of Hand, you have Disadvantage. On Success, you maneuver the item without being noticed.

upgrades.text: You may attempt to pick the pockets of NPCs and Mobs.
You may attempt to plant items on someone with pockets or the equivalent.
You may manipulate items up to half your own size (rounded down).

name: Smithing
desc: You may craft mundane items such as horseshoes, railroad spikes, nails, or the fun stuff: armor and weapons, but without DR or any bonuses (see Crafting, p. 221).

upgrades.text: You may craft items up to a +5 bonus.
You may craft items up to a +10 bonus.
Your crafting with this Skill takes half the time.

name: Stealth
limitations: You must be out of sight of all foes to begin this Check.
desc: Use this Skill if you want to move undetected or surprise a Mob. Make an INT-Opposed Skill Check. On Success before combat starts, you are unnoticed and gain 1 non-Attack Action (don't forget to take your 10ft Step). On Success in a non-combat situation, you remain unnoticed and can perform a Move Action with a 10ft Step as part of this Check.

upgrades.text: Your surprise Action can be an Attack with Advantage.
When other crawlers in your party roll this Skill untrained, they roll as normal (not with Disadvantage).
On a successful Surprise Check, you may also take a full Move and Step. If you Attack with your Surprise Action, deal x2 the base damage dice.

name: Streetwise
desc: Use this Skill in populated areas to learn or spread rumors, avoid attracting too much attention, gain access to less-than-legal items, and the like. Make an Unopposed Skill Check. On Success, you navigate a town without attracting attention, deal with a criminal network, identify an informal power structure, or gain the information you're seeking.

upgrades.text: You also hear an additional rumor, as determined by the GM. Or spread one!
You also quickly find a hiding place determined by the GM.
You also uncover information that might give you some leverage on an important person in town determined by the GM.

name: Survival
desc: You know how to survive in dangerous, often remote places for long periods of time with only the meager food and water you can rustle up. When traveling through such areas, make an Unopposed Skill Check. On Success, you survive the perils of the conditions unscathed. On a standard Fail, you suffer the effects of hunger and/or thirst (see p. 76).

upgrades.text: You do not suffer additional damage from a Critical Fail.
When other crawlers in your party roll this Skill untrained, they roll as normal (not with Disadvantage).
You do not suffer additional damage from a Major Fail.

name: Swimming
limitations: After 1 minute of Swimming (Success or Fail) or immediately on a Major Fail or worse, gain the Fatigued Debuff.
desc: Use this Skill when there are consequences for not swimming strongly or well rather than when you're taking a casual swim, such as racing for your life or swimming against a strong current. Make an Unopposed Skill Check every 30 seconds. On Success, you swim well despite the danger. For swimming during combat, see Special Forms of Movement, p. 70.

upgrades.text: After 2 minutes of Swimming (Success or Fail), gain the Fatigued Debuff.
You can swim at your full Move rate as an Action, but you still can't take a 10ft Step.
Make this Check every 5 minutes, and only gain the Fatigue Debuff on a Critical Fail.

name: Tactics
limitations: A crawler may attempt this Skill Check only once per combat.
desc: Your tactical mind and directions can spur your allies to victory. Choose one of the following combat disciplines: Attack, Damage, or Evade, and then make an Unopposed Skill Check. On Success, you and each member of your party gain a +1 bonus to Checks for the chosen discipline. Increase the bonus by +1 for each higher degree of Success.

upgrades.text: If you observe the foes and battlefield for at least 5 minutes prior to combat, roll this Skill Check with Advantage.
After using this Skill during a combat, you roll 2d10 when you Call a Play (still choose one die).
The bonus applies to all three combat disciplines instead of just one.

name: Tattoo Artistry
desc: Used to stick and poke ink under someone's skin to create a mundane tattoo. See Crafting, p. 221 for magical tattoos.

upgrades.text: You may craft tattoos with up to a +5 bonus.
You may craft tattoos with up to a +10 bonus.
Your crafting with this Skill takes half the time.

name: Taunt
desc: With a shout, some choice words, and maybe an obscene hand gesture, you attempt to draw the ire of enemies within 30 feet of you. After seeing where the Mob Attacks are headed, make an INT-Opposed Skill Check. On Success, Taunt one Attack of your choosing away from any target of your choosing and onto you. Higher degrees of Success allow you to Taunt additional Attacks onto you.

upgrades.text: You may make a free Evade Check against each Taunted Attack (roll separately vs. each Attack as usual). Then you may still spend an Action to Evade other Attacks and reroll any Fails from your free Evades.
You can affect Mobs within 60 feet.
Your free Evade Checks against Taunted Attacks are made with Advantage.

name: Throwing
desc: This Skill is used for passing the pigskin or throwing dynamite. You can Throw an object that weighs up to your STR in pounds at a distance of up to your STR x10 feet. To Throw a heavier or bulkier item (up to the GM's discretion), you do so with Disadvantage. To hit a target area, make an Unopposed Skill Check. To hit a foe with an object, make an Attack Skill Check vs. the target's Evade. On Success, you hit the target. On Fail, roll 1d8 for direction (see Figure 3); the amount the Skill Check missed by is the distance away in feet it lands.

upgrades.text: You have Advantage when Throwing to a target who wants to catch what you are selling.
Choose the direction on a miss, rather than roll.
Your Throw range is your STR x20 feet.

name: Tracking
desc: Use this Skill to find and follow tracks. When searching for or attempting to follow tracks, make an Unopposed Skill Check. Factors such as how long ago the tracks were made, the ground conditions, and whether other tracks or marks obscure them may influence the Difficulty. Once you find tracks, you must make another Tracking Check every 15 minutes to continue following them. On Success, you either find the tracks or continue following them.

upgrades.text: You can follow found tracks for 30 minutes before making a new Check, and gain 1 piece of information about the target(s).
You can follow found tracks for 1 hour before making a new Check, and gain 2 pieces of information about the target(s).
You can follow found tracks for 2 hours before making a new Check, and gain 4 pieces of information about the target(s).

name: Trap Engineer
desc: Used to craft traps via a Sapper's Table with a Trap Module (3,000 gold). See Crafting, p. 221.
